races.name: Bar 1 Betting Rated Novice Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Tell Us This
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good last time out (OR 111), giving it solid course claims; by nature a hold-up horse whose preferred rear-tracking role is compromised in a field this stacked with closers, so it is likely to race more prominently than ideal — watch whether Conor Stone-Walsh can settle it midfield and produce a clean jumping round.

runners_data.name: Cappa Hill
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner on OR (120) alongside several rivals and won on Good ground at 16f, but recent form (5th, 7th, 8th) shows a horse that has struggled for consistency; a genuine hold-up type that will need others to force the pace, which is unlikely given Luker's Tipple's lone-leader status — its race may hinge on the quality of its jumping.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's yard is in form (3/32 over 14 days) and Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride; has placed twice recently on similar Good ground and won over 17f here, but the 'F' in recent form is a jumping red flag for a novice chaser — naturally a hold-up horse that will drift toward midfield to find a position, with its chance relying on a clean round.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: The race's pace anchor — back-to-back wins over 18f on Good ground demonstrate both class and stamina for this trip; Gavin Cromwell's runner is fresh (7 days) and Keith Donoghue's booking is a positive flag, with the controlled front-running role suiting its profile perfectly if it reproduces recent form.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: Wears tp headgear (tongue plate) and has won twice but only on Soft ground, making this Good surface a material concern; a hold-up horse who finished 9th and 11th in her last two Good-ground starts, so the going profile is genuinely negative — Donagh Meyler will need a significant improvement in conditions suitability to get involved.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner (4/49 in 14 days, yard firing) has place form on Good ground over similar trips but has been finishing in the 3rd-7th range consistently — a hold-up type who needs a strong pace to reel in the leader, a scenario unlikely to materialise with only one confirmed front-runner controlling the race.

races.paceDynamic: Luker's Tipple is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner novice chase and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Keith Donoghue can dictate terms at whatever tempo he chooses over 1m7½f on Good ground at Tramore. That lone-leader dynamic creates a genuinely sustainable, controlled pace — Luker's Tipple has won back-to-back over this trip and ground and arrives in career-best form, making the front a formidable position. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types — Tell Us This, Cappa Hill, Killeemore Lad, Missus Beeton and Playtime — and while some will push forward to avoid being caught flat-footed, their natural instinct is to track or wait, meaning Luker's Tipple is unlikely to be harried early. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile: a lone pace-setter on Good ground over an honest novice chase trip who dictates without pressure is the classic template for a wire-to-wire performance. The field holds more hold-up types than can all race at the rear simultaneously — Tell Us This, Cappa Hill and Killeemore Lad are the three most likely to push forward into midfield to compensate, but none is a natural front-runner and none is expected to threaten Luker's Tipple's lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Luker's Tipple Leads Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Luker's Tipple secures the rail and controls a measured pace unchallenged from the outset.
scenarios.body: Donoghue dictates throughout, jumping efficiently and extending the lead from the second-last, leaving hold-up types with too much to do on Good ground. Luker's Tipple's back-to-back Good-ground wins over this trip confirm this shape suits it perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Challengers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Luker's Tipple sets only a crawl that bunches the field, allowing hold-up types to sprint past from the last.
scenarios.body: A false-pace scenario scrambles the race at the final fence, bringing the better-rated closers — Tell Us This (OR 111, recent winner) and Playtime — into contention with their finishing kicks. Gordon Elliott's Playtime and the Andrew McNamara-trained Tell Us This both have the form to capitalise if the front-runner is caught cold.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Force It
scenarios.trigger: If Killeemore Lad or Cappa Hill push aggressively into the slipstream and inject pace that weakens Luker's Tipple.
scenarios.body: Pressure on the leader across the far side tests Luker's Tipple's jumping and stamina, potentially opening the door for a well-held finisher to reel in a tiring leader after the last. Killeemore Lad's recent course form (2nd and 1st over similar trips on Good) makes it the most credible beneficiary if this scenario materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Falls/Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a fall disrupts the race order materially, reshuffling positions in a novice field with limited chasing experience.
scenarios.body: Novice chases at Tramore carry inherent jumping risk, and with Killeemore Lad having a fall in recent form (F in form string) the possibility of an incident cannot be dismissed. Missus Beeton, who has shown grit to win before and wears tp headgear, could be the unexpected beneficiary if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Watch Luker's Tipple's jumping at the final two fences — if it has built a clear lead, a mistake there is the primary threat to its chance in a novice contest.
Killeemore Lad has a fall in recent form; in a small-field novice chase, an early incident from this runner could disrupt the entire race order and alter the outcome dramatically.
Missus Beeton's going record on Good is 0 wins from 4 attempts versus 2 wins on Soft — if the ground rides on the faster side of Good, discount its chance accordingly.

Watch market moves on Tell Us This at the off — if punters back it into a short price it suggests stable confidence that its Good-ground course form will translate, regardless of the awkward tactical position it occupies in this race shape.

Monitor how aggressively Cappa Hill's jockey Sam Ewing positions early — if he pushes forward to chase Luker's Tipple rather than sitting back, it could inject pace that changes the entire complexion of what is otherwise a one-paced race shape.

races.name: O'Neill's Bar Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old prominent racer with solid Good-ground form (15 runs on similar going, two wins), he should secure a handy position early and his experience over this sort of trip makes him a logical danger if Le Kap is catchable late; 80 days off is a slight query but Bernard Martin Crowley sends him fit enough.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 108 marking him out as a leading contender; the chief concern is that unplaced run on his most recent start after 80 days off.

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Trainer Cian Collins has had a 1/15 strike-rate over 14 days, and Coded Welder arrives just 15 days after his last run showing recent form including a second on Good ground; the tongue-tie is noted and he is capable of holding a prominent position, though he has never won in 10 attempts on this going profile.|
runners_data.comment: Coded Welder shaped with promise when second three starts back and returns here on a quick 15-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; yet to win in recent starts, but he heads the ratings and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Freebie
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton (claimer, 7lb) teams up with trainer Adrian Sexton in what looks a family yard angle; two seconds in recent outings suggest a consistent but hard-to-win profile, and Good ground suits based on his sim-going record, though he has yet to win at the track on this surface.|
runners_data.comment: Frankie's Freebie has shown strong consistency at this level, second two and three starts back, and he returns on a quick 15-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going — the main risk is he remains winless in recent starts despite those near-misses.

runners_data.name: Happy Me
runners_data.note: Burke's charge is a genuine hold-up horse by style but finds itself mapped to midfield given the volume of rear-positioned types in this field; his form figures of 30-6P5 on Good ground are underwhelming and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 signals he is unlikely to get his preferred race, so discount his chances unless the pace is brutal.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Happy Me faces a stiff ask here; a pull-up in the run before last is the obvious concern, though today's going is familiar territory and 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Juke Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's representative has a 4/49 14-day trainer stat suggesting Elliott fires runners in good order, and the blinkers (hg:b) may sharpen him; he is a hold-up type who has finished fifth on three occasions without threatening, and Good ground is fine but he has never troubled the judge in six runs on similar conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of nine, Juke Hill at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on; 44 days between runs and a hefty 166 lb burden are the concerns here.

runners_data.name: Le Kap
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's confirmed front-runner is handled by Darragh O'Keeffe and should lead uncontested over this 2m6f, but a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 flags he has not always been able to fully exploit the lead role in terms of winning — zero wins from five runs on Good ground in his history is a concern despite controlling races.|

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old with visor (hg:v) and three career wins, he is a genuine hold-up specialist shuffled into the midfield mapping because the field overloads the rear; Gerard Keane's runner has run just 9 days ago and that quick turnaround alongside a declining recent form string (P-4700) makes it hard to construct a winning case here even in an attrition scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Mephisto has run over today's trip and going before, and at 166 lb carries significant weight, though nine days since his last run suggests he's fit and ready; the concern is a winless recent run of five starts that includes a pull-up.

runners_data.name: Rattledelatch
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fade flag that is consistent with his recent form (P0-960) and John Queally's 0/2 14-day record offers no trainer confidence boost; a hold-up type who has finished deep in the field repeatedly on Good ground, he faces an uphill battle in a shape that is unlikely to collapse fast enough for him to close.|
runners_data.comment: Rattledelatch is yet to win in his last five starts, but remains unexposed and open to improvement — 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, and the lightly raced profile leaves plenty of unknowns worth respecting at this level.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: The lightest horse in the field at 154lbs and the youngest at 4, Kasper Hauser is the most interesting hold-up type here with a recent win (1/19f/GOO) and placed form at short odds on Good ground; Calum Hogan claims 5lbs and Kevin Thomas Coleman has hit 2/16 over 14 days — worth monitoring if the pace quickens and the race becomes a stamina test.|
runners_data.comment: Kasper Hauser won last time out and returns after 20 days, with experience of today's going in his favour, but rated eighth of nine on our figures and carrying 154 lb, he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals here.

races.paceDynamic: Le Kap is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate at whatever tempo suits from the front, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good turf at Tramore. Behind him, Burru, Coded Welder, and Frankie's Freebie will push for prominent positions, creating a modestly competitive early scramble for the chasing berths but nothing that will genuinely pressurise Le Kap's lead. The hold-up contingent — Juke Hill, Rattledelatch, Kasper Hauser, and redistributed types Happy Me and Mephisto — will track from the rear, but with no strong pace-forcing dynamic, the gap back to the closers could be significant if Le Kap idles into a comfortable rhythm. This race shape heavily favours horses who can race prominently or track the leader closely without wasting energy, as a controlled front-running tempo on Good ground at this trip will reward jumping fluency and stamina over finishing kick; true hold-up horses face an uphill task if the pace is never truly honest. Happy Me and Mephisto are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield because the field carries more horses preferring rear positions than the race shape accommodates, with Le Kap and the prominent trio most likely to actually secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Le Kap Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Le Kap jumps fluently from the front and no rival applies sustained pressure through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: O'Keeffe settles Le Kap into a comfortable rhythm, controlling the tempo throughout and jumping the field into submission over the final mile; the honest Good ground rewards a horse who conserves energy in front rather than being pulled along by a rival. Prominent horses who can track within striking range of the leader without fuss are best placed to pounce if Le Kap tires late, but a fluent round of jumping from the front may prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Le Kap sets a sustainable clip but is caught flat-footed at the second-last as a prominent tracker lands with momentum.
scenarios.body: One of Burru, Coded Welder, or Frankie's Freebie tracks the leader closely throughout, conserving energy in a close second or third, then finds enough in the closing stages to reel in and pass Le Kap on the run-in. This suits horses with strong prominent profiles and solid records on Good ground, particularly those with recent course-distance experience at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Le Kap or the prominent pack set a genuinely brisk pace that strings the field out and creates a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop causes the front-runners to come back to the field in the final two fences, allowing a well-positioned hold-up horse to close with momentum through the distressed runners. Kasper Hauser, who has shown a recent win and is lightly weighted at 154lbs for a 4-year-old, is the most credible closer here if the race plays into this shape, though Juke Hill from the Elliott yard retains each-way claims.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Attrition Wins
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race shape early and the field loses all cohesion through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: With beginners steeplechasers, jumping mistakes can dramatically alter the complexion, removing front-runners or prominent horses and promoting unexpected winners; Mephisto has experience (age 9) and may navigate the chaos more composedly than younger rivals. This remains the least probable shape given the controlled dynamic and Good ground, but in a beginners' chase over 2m6f, attrition cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Le Kap's jumping under pressure — if he makes a significant error in the back straight he could capitulate quickly, handing the race to whoever is tracking closest, most likely Burru or Coded Welder.
Kasper Hauser is 4 years old stepping into a beginners' chase over 2m6f — green jumping at unfamiliar fences could cost him the race position he needs to utilise his finishing run.

Happy Me and Mephisto are both mapped out of their natural hold-up roles; if they are forced to race too prominently to compensate, they may do their racing too early and fade badly in the closing stages.
Mephisto runs just 9 days after his last outing — watch the market for any drift that signals the quick turnaround has left him short, as his form already shows a downward trend.

Rattledelatch's established fade pattern means he is a horse to use against in the betting rather than for — if he is prominent early, the fade flag suggests he will empty out before the final two fences.

races.name: McDonald & Son Builders Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Johnny Rambo
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form (2-1-F) over similar Good-ground trips makes him the most credible pace companion to Rosarian; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a bonus and his stamina looks solid over this 2m trip.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: Beaten a long way in every start and shows a tendency to fade in the finish; though mapped to midfield, this horse's true role is deep hold-up, which is the weakest position in today's steady-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Five outings without a win or place, form figures ugly across varying trips; held-up by inclination but placed into midfield on the map by necessity — today's shape does not suit a horse who needs a strong pace to weave through.

runners_data.name: Green Grass
runners_data.note: Single run to go on (13th over 2m4f on Good) and fades late; a genuine hold-up type with no evidence of the finishing kick needed when Rosarian controls the tempo from the front.

runners_data.name: I'm All In
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard has been firing (4/49 in 14 days) and this horse's prominent style is well-suited to the race shape; the U-pull and unplaced efforts are concerns but at this level his tactical position could paper over raw ability gaps.

runners_data.name: John Gun
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no public form to assess; Kieran Purcell runner with unknown style — one to watch in the market for market confidence that might signal inside knowledge.

runners_data.name: Pinkarizon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a PP9P form string and consistent good-ground runs but never threatens at the business end; Liam McKenna's 3lb claim helps on weight but the positional deficit in a steady-pace race is difficult to overcome.

runners_data.name: Spanish Rising
runners_data.note: Best of the hold-up brigade on form — a placed run over 2m+ on Good ground for Henry De Bromhead with Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong combination; needs things to go wrong up front to get involved but the profile is the most interesting among the closers.

runners_data.name: Faerie Tales
runners_data.note: Bumper form exclusively on Good ground but always finishing in double figures; a natural hold-up horse whose true position is at the rear, not the midfield slot the map assigns — Ben Kennedy's 7lb claim doesn't overcome the style mismatch today.

runners_data.name: Noble Rocco
runners_data.note: Two hurdle starts placing 9th and 7th over Good ground for Gordon Elliott; hold-up type who needs cut or a strong gallop — neither is on offer today — and Danny Gilligan faces a tough task from this position.

runners_data.name: Really Truly
runners_data.note: Completely unraced under Rules, Joseph O'Brien yard in form (7/61 in 14 days) and J J Slevin booked — the unknowns make this dangerous to dismiss, but the hold-up flag in headgear (h) and debut status mean it needs things to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: confirmed front-runner for Josh Halley with Danny Mullins aboard, second over 2m+ on Good ground on latest start — today's uncontested lead on a flat Good track at Tramore is almost exactly what this horse needs.

races.paceDynamic: Rosarian is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead, Danny Mullins can dictate a sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m trip on Good ground at Tramore. Johnny Rambo and I'm All In are the only other prominent-style horses likely to sit close, creating a small lead group ahead of a congested midfield. The majority of the field — Green Grass, Pinkarizon, Spanish Rising, Noble Rocco, and those redistributed to midfield — are hold-up types who will need the pace to collapse late, which an uncontested Rosarian is unlikely to allow. This race shape strongly favours the lead-to-prominent profile: a horse travelling comfortably on or just off the pace has the clearest path to victory, as genuine hold-up types will face a stern test of finishing relish on a track where Rosarian's controlled tempo gives nothing away for free. Note that Faerie Tales, Devine Genius, and Folk Warrior are true hold-up horses shuffled forward on the pace map simply because the rear of the field is over-subscribed — none of them is likely to secure the prominent position shown, making the closer scenario structurally weaker than raw numbers suggest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosarian Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rosarian bowls along in front at a fair but controlled clip and no rival has the pace or inclination to seriously press for the lead.
scenarios.body: Danny Mullins sets the fractions to suit, the field strings out behind him, and a horse travelling powerfully within itself approaching the final hurdle will be very hard to reel in on this flat finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field but a prominent tracker has more gears than Rosarian turning for home.
scenarios.body: Johnny Rambo or I'm All In, close enough throughout, is best placed to challenge the leader at the last and exploit any signs of Rosarian tiring; a horse who has been competitive over similar distances on Good ground is the type to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Up
scenarios.trigger: If Rosarian goes too fast early — even fractionally — and the leaders hit the wall inside the final two hurdles, leaving a gap for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Spanish Rising, who showed clear improvement stepping up to 2m+ on Good ground, or Really Truly representing Joseph O'Brien from an unexposed profile, could sweep through a tiring lead group; this scenario is structurally discounted because the pace is expected to be sustainable, not pressurised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart / Scrappy Outcome
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, unseats or jumping errors disrupt the race and an otherwise out-of-contention runner inherits a position it couldn't earn on merit.
scenarios.body: Chaotic jumping in a 12-runner maiden hurdle can scramble the race shape entirely, and a horse like Noble Rocco or John Gun (unknown style, lightly raced) could benefit from attrition rather than tactical superiority.

watchPoints.text: Rosarian — if Danny Mullins bowls along uncontested and jumps cleanly, the horse who beats him must come from the prominent group, not the rear; watch whether any rival makes a move to close at the top of the home straight.

Really Truly — completely unexposed for Joseph O'Brien with J J Slevin; debut runners from this yard with top jockeys can spring surprises and the market move at the off is the most important clue available.

John Gun — another runner with zero public form and an unknown style flag; Donagh Meyler is an experienced conditional and if this horse shows natural pace it could disrupt the expected Rosarian-led shape.

I'm All In — the two unseats in recent form are a jumping flag worth tracking at the early hurdles; if he gets round cleanly his prominent style suits the race shape, but a repeat exit would drastically thin the field and change the dynamics.

Faerie Tales and Devine Genius — both mapped ahead of their natural position due to the congested hold-up group; if either drops back to their true held-up role early, it is a sign the race shape is playing out exactly as projected and the prominent horses will not be run at.

races.name: Flynn Hotel Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Churchwarden
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 108 for De Bromhead, a hold-up horse who found trouble on his last run (two Ps) but boasts a course win and has solid form on Good ground; blinkers applied and a 37-day freshener may sharpen his finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Churchwarden landed a win four starts back and was second five starts back, showing he holds genuine form at this level, and he returns fit on 37 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions; the worry is his two pulled-up efforts since that win.

runners_data.name: Palace Boy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type back quickly after just 10 days, with modest similar-going form (0W1P from 4 runs) and an OR slipping to 107; Keith Donoghue's booking is the main positive, but stamina questions over 2m on recent evidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Palace Boy nonetheless shaped with promise when second four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; rated 117, he holds solid claims despite the 165 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter and clear shape-controller here; his natural style is prominent/front-running and he fits the race perfectly, but five recent runs show a tendency to finish second rather than close out — watch for a hold-up horse reeling him in late if stamina wavers.|
runners_data.comment: Dairy Force arrives here in decent nick, twice finishing second in his last three starts and returning after just 17 days, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the worry is that he remains winless in recent starts and must shoulder 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose chart position in midfield reflects redistribution rather than true preference; trainer Connell has no runners in the 14-day window and the horse's 11 recent runs on Good have all produced modest finishes — the STYLE_FIT discount is warranted.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back shows Claude has ability at this level, and he returns fit on 17 days' rest having run over today's trip and going before — our rating of 113 underlines his claims; the main risk is a patchy recent record, winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's runner is a true hold-up type shunted forward on the map due to field congestion at the rear; raced just 5 days ago and returned a solid 2W6P record on Good ground over this trip, but racing back-to-back off a short turnaround is a physical query for a hold-up horse needing a finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Rightfolksplease ran well enough to win last time out and has placed experience over today's trip and conditions, but carrying 158 lb for a gelding ranked fifth of six on our figures makes him hard to fancy at this level despite that recent confidence-booster.

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Carries the bottom weight at OR 94 and is flagged as fading in the finish — a recurring pattern in form — returning from 78 days off; a true hold-up type remapped to midfield, but without a win or place from five Good-ground runs, this profile needs chaos rather than a fair-run race to feature.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts — which include an unseating and two unplaced efforts — Kome Dans Un Reve is hard to fancy here; our rating has him ranked last of six, and 78 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Dairy Force is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, is positioned to dictate terms at whatever tempo suits connections — on Good ground at Tramore over 2m, that is likely to be a controlled, measured gallop that keeps the race in his own hands. The five hold-up horses behind — Churchwarden, Palace Boy, Claude, Rightfolksplease, and Kome Dans Un Reve — will be forced to settle and cover ground, with the closers needing a meaningful late injection of pace to reel in a horse allowed to bowl along unchallenged. This field is dominated by genuine hold-up types: Claude, Rightfolksplease, and Kome Dans Un Reve are all true rearward runners who have been mapped to midfield purely because there is insufficient prominent cover in this field for all of them to operate from their natural berth. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racer with stamina — specifically Dairy Force front and alone — or a hold-up horse with the class to accelerate hardest off a sustainable gallop; Churchwarden and Palace Boy, the two least constrained hold-up types in this field, are best positioned to deliver that challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dairy Force Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Dairy Force bowls clear from the gate and is allowed a soft lead throughout, setting a gallop that suits his stamina profile.
scenarios.body: Dairy Force dictates every yard, controls the tempo, and has enough in reserve on Good ground to repel closers who have been held up and must make up ground on a horse that has never been asked to race. The prominent-racer profile is tailor-made for this shape, and his five recent top-two finishes over this distance band underline his ability to win from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sustainable and a hold-up horse produces a clean round of jumping and a decisive late burst.
scenarios.body: Churchwarden, carrying blinkers for De Bromhead and returning from a 37-day break, has the class at OR 108 and a win over this course-and-distance-band in similar going to make a telling late challenge. Palace Boy, fresh off a 10-day turnaround, is the other hold-up type with a realistic profile to pick up the pieces if Dairy Force flattens out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Midfield Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply and the redistributed midfield hold-up horses find themselves closer than expected at a crucial stage.
scenarios.body: Claude and Rightfolksplease are both racing out of their natural role mapped to midfield, and if jumping errors or positional chaos compresses the field, one could emerge in a better spot than typical. However, both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and their trainer form is minimal, limiting confidence in this scenario converting.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Outsider Poaches
scenarios.trigger: If the race is disrupted by jumping mishaps, interference, or an unexpected collapse in the front-runner, scrambling the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: Kome Dans Un Reve, despite a fading-in-finish flag and 78 days off the track, carries the lowest weight and could steal a messy race if the pace implodes spectacularly. This scenario is marginal and relies on multiple things going wrong for the principals ahead of her in the market.

watchPoints.text: Watch Dairy Force's jumping at the early hurdles — if he makes errors under Danny Gilligan, the solo front-runner loses his key advantage and the race immediately opens up for the hold-up horses.

Rightfolksplease ran only five days ago; monitor how Kevin Healy (7) manages him in the first mile, as a horse running back-to-back off a hold-up style needing a late run is at risk of having nothing left when it matters.

Churchwarden's last two runs were both pulls-up (PP), and despite the De Bromhead booking of Darragh O'Keeffe there is a question over whether his jumping has fully recovered — watch him at the early obstacles closely.

Kome Dans Un Reve's 78-day absence combined with a confirmed fading-in-finish pattern makes her a horse to watch drifting through the field in the closing stages rather than making ground — she may be an in-running lay if prominent early.

With Claude, Rightfolksplease, and Kome Dans Un Reve all true hold-up types forced into midfield positions, any tactical crowding on the bend could create positional traffic — watch for interference among the redistributed trio as they seek racing room.|

races.paceDynamic: Master Haku is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse to set the tempo in a seven-runner field, he is almost certain to get a comfortable lead and control fractions from the front over this 2m4½f trip on Good ground at Tramore. Early Dawning, Mr Master Mac, and Lureka Du Noyer are all prominent types who will press for position behind him, creating a compact but organised shape rather than a frantic pace — Master Haku dictates but is unlikely to be left entirely alone. Holy Joe and Siege Of Carthage are the genuine hold-up operators and will be produced late off what should be a measured, even gallop. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in a controlled rhythm and quicken off honest fractions — true hold-up horses will need the pace to genuinely collapse late, which a lone front-runner at a sustainable tempo is unlikely to provide. The field contains more prominent types than can all settle in that position, with Master Haku certain to take the front and Early Dawning and Lureka Du Noyer the most likely to lock in the best early positions behind him; Mr Master Mac may be pushed wider or further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Master Haku Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Master Haku leads unchallenged at a sustainable clip and the prominent runners behind him track in orderly fashion without disrupting the tempo.
scenarios.body: Master Haku controls proceedings from the front, the pace is honest but not gruelling, and horses that travel prominently in the first half of the race arrive at the last with enough energy to fight out the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the honest pace set by Master Haku stretches the field sufficiently that genuine hold-up horses get rolling late and mow down tired prominent runners.
scenarios.body: Holy Joe or Siege Of Carthage are produced with one sweeping run from the back straight, arriving with momentum as the leaders empty inside the final two hurdles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Ignites
scenarios.trigger: If the competitive instincts of Early Dawning, Mr Master Mac, and Lureka Du Noyer push the tempo beyond what Master Haku intended and the race becomes a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A fierce mid-race battle develops, burning off those who pressed too hard, and a horse who drops in slightly from the front — or a hold-up type — benefits from the resulting attrition in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Butch Coolidge Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Butch Coolidge, a natural prominent type remapped to midfield, manages to work forward and secure a position closer than his mapped role suggests.
scenarios.body: Racing at a mark of 102 he carries less weight and could travel economically if he finds a rhythm close enough to the pace; the weight advantage becomes meaningful if the race is truly run.

watchPoints.text: Watch Master Haku's early gallop — if Sam Ewing lets him stride clear unchallenged in the first mile, the race is almost certainly set to be run exactly to the front-runner's strengths and the hold-up horses face a very difficult task.

Monitor Early Dawning and Lureka Du Noyer in the first half-mile; if both press hard behind Master Haku and the pace quickens significantly, the race could develop into a stamina test that reshapes the likely beneficiaries entirely.

Butch Coolidge's starting price relative to his OR of 102 deserves attention — if he drifts markedly in the market it likely confirms he is unable to secure a forward position and is effectively racing out of role.

Siege Of Carthage's unbeaten run when completing on Good ground (1W1P from 3 Good runs) is a positive, but the pulled-up run in his most recent form should be contextualised before treating him as a confident hold-up play.

The trainer 14-day figures for both Gordon Elliott runners (4/49) and Henry de Bromhead (4/37) are moderate — neither yard is firing at a high short-term strike rate, which is worth factoring into confidence levels on Master Haku, Holy Joe, and Lureka Du Noyer.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Logic is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and will dictate from the front over 2m4½f on good ground at Tramore, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead early. Double Power and Jack Inthe Jukebox are mapped prominent but neither has the profile or current form to seriously contest the front rank, meaning Pure Logic should enjoy an uncontested lead through the early and middle stages. The overwhelming majority of this field are hold-up or midfield types — Inchidaly Copper, Diamond Secret, Colesberg, Maxicourt, Nashville Notions, Taketwotoone, Beacon Bypass and others — and with so many genuine closers competing for the same ground late, the race will funnel into a mass cavalry charge from the home turn. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a steady pace over a strongly-run distance — moderately favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained run from two out, but the sheer congestion of closers risks splitting the benefits: horses who can travel sweetly in mid-division and pick their way through traffic, or the leader who builds an unassailable advantage, are the primary beneficiaries. The field contains far more hold-up types than can genuinely race from the rear — Nashville Notions, Taketwotoone, Beacon Bypass, Miss Guiry, The Ducks Walk, Keep The Head, Talas Kera, Princess Felicia, The Cobblers Wife and Youknowme have all been redistributed to midfield, with those best-placed early in the pack — Inchidaly Copper and Diamond Secret — most likely to secure a clean passage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Logic Dictates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Logic is allowed a soft lead and controls the pace throughout, building an advantage that the hold-up pack cannot close.
scenarios.body: Pure Logic, uncontested at the front on good ground over a trip it handles, sets a gallop that is comfortable enough to preserve energy yet fast enough to strand a congested chasing group who cannot coordinate their challenge; the jockey Danny Mullins can manage the fractions exactly as he wishes with no rival applying pressure. A prominent-handy type who travels into the race rather than chasing is best placed, and any horse lying within three to five lengths of the leader at the second-last will be favoured over deep closers mired in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Power Through Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field and a handful of hold-up horses find a clear run from two out to overwhelm a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners and a single front-runner setting an honest but unforced gallop, the peloton concertinas approaching the home straight and horses with the best positioning inside the final half-mile — particularly those who have held prominent midfield slots rather than being trapped deep — produce the most sustained finish. Inchidaly Copper brings strong good-ground form at this trip and has three wins and seven places from 15 good-ground starts, making it the standout closer profile; Diamond Secret, though held up, has the class to pick off tiring rivals if given a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, First Prompt Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of hold-up types creates a gridlock in the straight and an alert prominently-placed horse pounces before the cavalry arrives.
scenarios.body: In a field this large with so many genuine closers all seeking the same late ground, the first horse to commit turning for home — one already within striking distance of Pure Logic — can steal a march as the closers are hampered, checked or simply run out of room. Double Power, despite a fade flag and poor recent form, is mapped prominent and would benefit from this shape; Jack Inthe Jukebox similarly sits in a useful position if the traffic chaos freezes the chasing group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Logic goes too fast early for a good-ground 2m4½f hurdle and the field sweeps past in the final flight.
scenarios.body: Should Pure Logic overcook it — unlikely given the style-fit flag and Mullins's experience — the race opens for the deepest closers, but this scenario is markedly less probable because so many of the horses who would benefit are redistributed types not truly racing from their natural hold-up position; their style-fit discounts apply in full. Beacon Bypass and Talas Kera have the profile on paper but both carry style-fit penalties and poor recent form, severely limiting confidence in this shape materialising cleanly.

races.paceDynamic: Dream On Baby is the sole confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride off from the gates and dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Tramore's flat 2m circuit. Fraher Field, Ma Belle Etoile, Paul's Dream, and Thisistheway will press into prominent positions just behind her, creating a bunched, competitive group rather than a strung-out procession. The field carries more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Kimy and Silas Marner, both true sit-and-wait horses, are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than they would choose as the pack compresses. With one uncontested front runner setting a measured tempo, the race shape favours prominent racers who can travel in the slipstream and produce a sustained late effort, rather than genuine deep closers who need a strong gallop to reel horses in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream On Baby Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Dream On Baby is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace never truly quickens until after the final turn.
scenarios.body: Dream On Baby sets a comfortable gallop that suits her proven front-running style, and the prominent group behind her — Paul's Dream, Fraher Field, Thisistheway — get the perfect pitch to pounce in the straight without burning energy early; this is the dominant shape given one confirmed pace-setter and a bunched, non-pressuring chasing pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Surge Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger mid-race and the front group swamps Dream On Baby turning for home.
scenarios.body: Paul's Dream, who has won at this trip on Good ground, and Thisistheway, with solid course-similar form, are ideally placed to overtake a tiring Dream On Baby in the final quarter-mile; this rewards horses who sit second or third and travel smoothly throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop unexpectedly quickens mid-race and the leaders empty out, leaving a late gap for genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Run For Mahler and Splashing Out, legitimate hold-up horses who won over similar distances on Good ground, would have the most to gain if the pace collapses in front of them; however this scenario is discounted because Kimy and Silas Marner — the redistributed hold-up horses most likely to be pushed forward — are not true deep closers in this configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Dream On Baby quickens with two furlongs to run and the prominent group is caught flat-footed chasing.
scenarios.body: Dream On Baby has placed consistently at shorter trips on Good going and her headgear suggests she is capable of a sharp effort; with an uncontested lead she could simply extend before rivals can organise a challenge, though her recent form string of placed efforts suggests she finds one or two.

watchPoints.text: Dream On Baby's uncontested lead could make this a one-horse race if she dictates fully — watch whether any prominent horse such as Paul's Dream or Thisistheway applies early pressure or concedes her a clear rail advantage unchallenged.

Kimy and Silas Marner are being pushed out of their natural hold-up roles into mid-division — if they are restless or awkward early, they could unsettle the pack immediately behind Dream On Baby and artificially quicken the gallop sooner than expected.

Paul's Dream has won four times on Good going at 16-20f but her last two runs include a 13th at 20f on Heavy — watch for any sign in the market or early running that she is not moving as well as her form profile suggests.

With seven amateur/claimer jockeys in an 11-runner field on a flat track, positional errors or wide draws could compress the mid-pack significantly in the first quarter-mile — Fraher Field and Ma Belle Etoile are the prominent types most likely to be squeezed if a rough early pace develops.

Run For Mahler won at 20f on Good turf and has the cleanest hold-up profile in the field — if she obtains a clear run into the straight without being blocked by the redistributed mid-packers, she represents the most credible late-challenge threat to the prominent group.
